articles.title: Eye on Everything
articles.summary: The SJAA board has reinstated a member directory and welcomed new board members Ed Erbeck and Terry Kahl. The association also joined the International Dark Sky Association (IDA) to address light pollution, encouraging members to get involved. Upcoming events include a swap meet/auction in April and an astrophotography talk in May, with an apology for previous speaker scheduling issues.

articles.title: Activities Calendar
articles.summary: This document outlines a calendar of astronomy-related activities for March and April, primarily organized by an astronomy group. Events include numerous star parties at various locations, an observational astronomy class, a general meeting featuring a speaker, and a Bay-Area Swap Meet and Auction. The calendar also notes the start of Daylight Saving Time and AANC Astronomy Day.

articles.title: Election of Board of Directors
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) held its Board of Directors election at the General Meeting on February 22, 1997. Five directors were elected or re-elected for two-year terms, while four directors have one year remaining in their terms. Lew Kurtz retired from the Board but will continue to assist with the SJAA Ephemeris.

articles.title: The Summer Milky Way in DARK skies!
articles.summary: This article announces the 4th Annual Mount Lassen Volcanic National Park Star Party, hosted by Ptolemy's Supper Club from July 3-6, 1997, coinciding with a new Moon. The event emphasizes deep-sky observing under exceptionally dark skies, offering group camping at Lost Creek, a communal dinner, and both private and public star party sessions. Attendees are encouraged to reserve their spots for camping and dinner by sending payment to Mark Wagner, with returning participants having priority.

articles.title: Jim Van Nuland
articles.summary: Star parties at Henry Coe State Park are undergoing two major changes. Starting in April, the observation site will move from the current knoll to a parking lot, as the knoll is being repurposed for a Ranger's residence. Additionally, attendees will now be required to pay a $5 day-use fee per vehicle, or a $30 group fee for more than six people, as the previous 'free event' justification is no longer accepted by park management.

articles.title: Jim Van Nuland
articles.summary: The schoolyard star party program is experiencing ongoing success, attracting hundreds of attendees at events in January and February. A busy schedule of upcoming star parties for March and April at various schools in the San Jose area is provided. The article concludes with a call for volunteers to assist with these educational outreach events.

articles.title: Eye, continued from page 1
articles.summary: The article details upcoming events for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) including a picnic, various speaker nights, and a 'Slide and Equipment night' in September. It also announces a beginning astrophotography class, seeks volunteers for a Lunar and Planetary observing class, and notes the passing of former SJAA board member Bob Madden. The editor is also stepping down, and a new SJAA website is available.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: This article provides an update on Comet Hale-Bopp, detailing its excellent visibility in the morning sky and improving evening view as it approaches perihelion on April 1, encouraging readers to observe this spectacular comet. It also announces the discoveries of three new comets: C/1997 A1 (NEAT), P/1997 B1 (Kobayashi), and C/1997 O1 (Gehrels), briefly describing each. Additionally, it mentions upcoming total solar and partial lunar eclipses.

articles.title: Ephemerides - Epoch 2000, 0h UTC
articles.summary: This document provides detailed ephemerides for three comets: C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp), 46P/Wirtanen, and 81P/Wild 2, for the period of March-April 2000, referenced to Epoch 2000, 0h UTC. It includes tables specifying their Right Ascension, Declination, Elongation, and Sky Magnitude, alongside a separate table detailing their orbital elements like perihelion date, distance, inclination, and orbital period.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar - Mar 1997
articles.summary: This document is a celestial calendar for March 1997, providing comprehensive astronomical data for observers. It details lunar phases, rise and set times, and celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination) for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. Additionally, it includes information on astronomical twilight, sidereal time, and highlights the darkest Saturday night of the month for optimal viewing.

articles.title: Astro Ads
articles.summary: This document features 'Astro Ads,' a free classifieds section for noncommercial sales of astronomically related products. Several used and new items are listed, including Celestron binoculars and telescopes, a Takahashi APO refractor, and a Pyrex glass mirror blank. Additionally, it provides instructions for submitting new ads and encourages members to submit articles for publication in the SJAA Ephemeris newsletter.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program Status
articles.summary: This document provides a status update for a telescope loaner program, detailing the availability and current borrowing status of various telescopes. It lists specific models, borrowers, due dates, and includes notes regarding special conditions for certain instruments and a waiting list. Members of the SJAA are invited to contact the program to borrow available scopes.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the officers and board of directors, along with their contact numbers, for an organization, presumably SJAA based on the footer. It also details the chairpersons and members for various committees and programs such as the Mentoring Program, Observatory Committee, and Telescope Loaner Program, providing a comprehensive directory of key personnel.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing membership fees ($15 for regular, $6 for junior) and an optional add-on subscription to Sky & Telescope magazine ($27). It provides instructions for payment via check to "SJAA" and submission either in person at a meeting or by mail to the treasurer. The form also includes contact and mailing address information for the association.
